title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 12
paragraphs: After the desires of both had been fulfilled, they set off for what they had chosen. At this same time it happened that Darius saw something that made him want to order Megabazus to conquer the Paeonians and forcibly remove them from Europe into Asia. The matter was this. There were certain Paeonians named Pigres and Mantyes who, when Darius had crossed over into Asia, came to Sardis because they themselves wished to rule over the Paeonians, and with them they brought their sister, who was tall and beautiful. Then, having watched for a time when Darius was holding public audience in the suburb of the Lydian city, they dressed their sister up as well as they could and sent her off to fetch water, with a water-jar on her head, leading a horse after her by a bridle wound around her arm, and at the same time spinning flax. As the woman passed by him on her way out of the city, Darius took notice of the matter, for what the woman was doing was not Persian or Lydian fashion, nor indeed the manner of any people of Asia. So he sent some of his spearmen with orders to watch what the woman would do with the horse. They followed her; and having come to the river, she watered the horse, and having watered him and filled her jar with water, she came back along the same road, carrying the water on her head, leading the horse after her by the bridle round her arm, and at the same time turning the spindle.
